rationale: The evaluator feedback highlights that the current sensor_weights have strong negative values (-1.0) on the outer sensors, which may cause overcorrection and increase steering oscillation. To address this, I reduced the magnitude of the negative weights on the outer sensors from -1.0 to -0.7 to soften the correction and improve stability. The sensor_size was 0.012, a medium size; since no telemetry was provided yet to confirm noise robustness, I increased sensor_size to 0.016 to improve signal stability and reduce noise impact. The line_loss strategy was 'search_left'; the evaluator suggested considering 'last_direction' if line loss events remain high. To proactively improve recovery robustness, I changed line_loss to 'last_direction' to allow the robot to search in the last known direction of the line, which should help in complex track shapes and reduce line loss events. I kept the PID gains unchanged (kp=0.9, ki=0.05, kd=0.15) as no telemetry indicated they were problematic yet. I request telemetry measurements on completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, and noise_robustness to verify if these changes reduce oscillation, improve line recovery, and enhance noise robustness as expected.
